title: NVIDIA and Lambda Disclose First Production Co-Packaged Optics Cluster... It is FINALLY real
gist: NVIDIA and Lambda disclosed at SC26 the first production co-packaged optics cluster (10,000+ GPUs on Quantum-X CPO switches), showing CPO is deployed now rather than years away. Pluggable, serviceable light sources and lower switch power (freeing watts for GPUs) are the key enablers; the open question is the adoption curve.

insights.claim: Lambda has deployed NVIDIA co-packaged optics (CPO) switching in production in a cluster of more than 10,000 GPUs, disclosed at SC26, contradicting industry views that CPO is still years away.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: CPO timelines are pulled forward; optics and switch suppliers' roadmaps assuming late CPO adoption may be mispriced.
insights.quote: Lambda has already deployed it in production in a cluster with over 10,000 GPUs
insights.locator: For SC26, NVIDIA and Lambda discussed

insights.claim: The author notes that at OCP Summit 2026 another vendor's keynote claimed CPO was still years from deployment, illustrating that industry consensus lagged NVIDIA's actual production deployment.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Competitor messaging understating CPO readiness signals NVIDIA's lead over rival networking vendors.
insights.quote: I heard during another vendor’s keynote that CPO was still years away from deployment

insights.claim: With CPO now deployed in production, the key open question for the industry shifts from whether or when CPO ships to the shape of its adoption curve.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Track CPO attach rates in AI clusters as the next indicator for pluggable-optics demand displacement.
insights.quote: The big question now is what the adoption curve will be.

insights.claim: NVIDIA's first-generation co-packaged optics ship in its Quantum-X (InfiniBand) switching product, with Spectrum-X to follow as an updated second-generation CPO part.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Spectrum-X CPO is the next product step that would extend CPO into NVIDIA's Ethernet line.
insights.locator: We covered NVIDIA’s co-packaged optics extensively

insights.claim: NVIDIA's Quantum-X CPO switch provides 144 MPO/MTP ports at 800Gbps each, fed by an array of 18 pluggable light sources on the front of the chassis.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Quantifies how CPO replaces 144 pluggable optical modules per switch, a direct hit to transceiver unit volumes.

insights.claim: Making CPO laser light sources pluggable and field-serviceable removed a key historical inhibitor to CPO in switches, because light sources are the components that most often fail in optics.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Serviceability resolves a major operator objection to CPO, raising adoption odds for hyperscalers and neoclouds.
insights.quote: Light sources tend to be the parts that fail in pluggable optics, so making them serviceable was an important innovation.
insights.locator: NVIDIA is using an array of 18

insights.claim: Using 18 light sources instead of 144 800G optical modules (or 72 dual-800G modules) means a CPO switch has fewer failure-prone light sources than a traditional switch and is easier to cool.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Reliability and thermal advantages strengthen CPO's TCO case versus pluggable transceivers.

insights.claim: Moving optics onto the switch package eliminates long high-speed copper electrical traces from the switch chip to front-panel cages, significantly lowering switch power consumption.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Lower network power is a structural driver for CPO in power-constrained AI datacenters.

insights.claim: In power-limited AI datacenters, network power saved by CPO can be redirected to GPUs, so more GPUs fit in the same footprint and revenue per watt of cluster power rises.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Frames CPO as a revenue lever for GPU cloud operators like Lambda, not just a cost saving; supports NVIDIA networking attach.
insights.quote: the more power that can be used for GPUs directly impacts the revenue that can be generated per Watt of power available to the cluster
